subject: Filtering by metadata other than population

messages.author: e64f7bb1494774f9
messages.subject: Filtering by metadata other than population
parts:
Firstly, thank you for developing this R package! I have found it extremely helpful so far!


I have a question about “Using R commands to manipulate genlight objects” (Section 9.6 in your dartR manual).


How would you filter your data based on other metadata (e.g. not by population)?


An example using your provided dataset:


gl <- gl.read.dart(filename= testset.gl, ind.metafile = testset_metadata.csv,, probar=FALSE)


In your test metadata file, you have “sex” with 3 levels: Male, Female and Unknown.


What if you only want to analyse your SNP data for only Females? Based on the pdf, you could do the following:


gl_fem <- gl[gl@other$ind.metrics$sex!=c("Male", “Unknown”), ]


However, the pdf says that this will result in only subsetting metadata but not metadata for all loci.


“To take care for the correct filtering for loci and individuals we suggest therefore to use the following approach:”


You would then have to do the following operations to have the loci file match the metadata file.

index.ind <- pop(gl)=="EmmacRussEube" | pop(gl)=="EmvicVictJasp"

table( pop(gl), index.ind)

index.loc <- sample(nLoc(gl), 30, replace = F)

glsub2 <- gl[index.ind, index.loc]

glsub2@other$ind.metrics <- gl@other$ind.metrics[index.ind,] #not necessary

glsub2@other$loc.metrics <- gl@other$loc.metrics[index.loc,] #necessary


However, this is tailored to population filtering. Could you please provide an example where you do the same operation but for other metadata (“sex” for example)? 


Thank you!

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Filtering by metadata other than population
parts:
Hi Kate,

The safest way to do this would be

pop(gl) <- gl@other$ind.metrics$sex
gl.fem <- gl.keep.pop(gl,pop.list="Female")

This would overwrite your populations assignments. If you wanted to keep them, use

gl@other$ind.metrics$popid <- pop(x) # Save the population assignments in new variable popid
pop(gl) <- gl@other$ind.metrics$sex # Assign sex to the pop variable
gl.fem <- gl.keep.pop(gl,pop.list="Female") # Delete all individuals except those with pop = Female
pop(gl) <- gl@other$ind.metrics$popid # Recover the population assignments

By doing this, you will take advantage of dartR managing the idiosyncrasies of genlight objects behind the scenes.

Hope this helps.

A

Hi Kate,

I have coded this in now, and ability to specify a different individual metric as a basis for dropping/keeping will be in the next release. In the meantime, you might like to load the attached scripts.

To do what you want, now use

gl <- gl.keep.pop(testset.gl, pop.list="Male", as.pop="sex", verbose=3)

or similar. You can be my tester :)

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: Filtering by metadata other than population
parts:
Hi Kate,

With the filtering of monomorphs, a number of people asked that this not be done automatically, as they wanted to keep them in there, and it was an action that could not be undone. You can force the filtering of monomorphs by setting mono.rm=TRUE (in earlier versions this was the default).

With the recalculation function, it is very computationally expensive, so you do not really want it to do it over and over as you work through a series of filters, so the idea is that the metrics are not recalculated each time by default, giving you the option to recalculated them at the end of the filtering with gl.recalc.metrics.  You can force the recalculation of locus metrics by setting recalc=TRUE (in earlier versions this was the default).

The script warns you so that you are clear on the status of these options.

We are working on a mechanism for trapping status in terms of whether there are monomorphs present, or out of date locus metrics (as global options), to improve management of this. Hopefully, that will be behind the scenes and not affect your pipelines.

Sorry for chopping and changing on this. I understand that this means some of your established pipelines will break. Hopefully, dartR will settle down soon re these sorts of changes.

A
